# The Planet That Wanders Home

## Scripture

*"Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence? If I go up to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in the depths, you are there."* — Psalm 139:7-8

## Reflection

This month, if you find a clear eastern sky before dawn, you may spot a brilliant point of light near the constellation Gemini—Jupiter, the wandering star. Unlike the fixed stars that hold their places, Jupiter drifts through the zodiac over months, brightening and dimming, appearing in different corners of the sky each season. Ancient astronomers called such lights "planets," from the Greek for "wanderer."

Perhaps you know what it is to wander. To feel far from where you meant to be—far from home, far from God, far from the person you hoped to become. The autumn sky itself seems to wander: the sun sinks lower each day, the stars rise earlier, and even the brightest lights move through the dark.

Yet Jupiter never truly leaves its orbit. It wanders *within* a path that holds it, governed by a gravity it cannot see but cannot escape. So it is with us. David asks, "Where can I flee from your presence?"—and the answer is nowhere, because there is nowhere God is not. The heavens cannot contain Him, and the depths cannot hide us from Him. Even our wandering is held.

If this season finds you drifting, take heart. The God who set Jupiter in its course has set His love upon you. You are not lost to Him. You are only ever held.

## Prayer

Father, when I wander, remind me that Your hand still holds me. I cannot flee from Your presence, and I am grateful. Guide my drifting heart home to You. In Jesus' name, amen.
